The HTTP standard includes many features beyond those shown in this one simple example. To illustrate just one more, consider sending another request, similar to the first but with one additional header:

```
GET/+max/HTTP/1.1
Host:www.gustavus.edu
If-none-match:W/"30ba07-b94-21857f40"
```

This time, the reply from the web server is much shorter:

```
HTTP/1.1304NotModified
Date:Sun,16Jan200501:19:55GMT
Server:Apache
Connection:close
```</previous>
<target>##### `ETag: W/"30ba07-b94-21857f40"`

This corresponds with the scenario described in Section 9.1.2. The browser (or a human using `telnet` to simulate a browser) is asking “please send this web page only if it has changed since the version I previously downloaded.” The version is identified using the _ETag_ ( _entity tag_ ) the server provided when it sent the previous version. In this case, the version on the server still is the same (matches the provided tag), so the server just sends a short reply to that effect. A browser could use this to validate continuing to use a cached copy.</target>
